final_assessment: Sal retired Q-rc04-d as a false distinction and he was right; checking the trail rather than arguing settled it against my framing. I had asked whether the readiness record is WRITTEN at the archive or RENDERED from a judgement formed earlier, recommending rendering on the argument that authorship at the seam produced rc02c's 3,333 characters of warnings prose. Sal's answer was that the flow already works the way I was proposing: at decision points we judge from the data, record it, move on, and at archive the records exist so we summarize and emit. The trail confirms it — walk decisions across rc02c's cycle carry ratified_via, recommendation_fork.chosen and a verbatim resolution, nine of them, structured and readable back, because orbit-address-reviews was built for exactly that. What the trail ALSO shows is the thing I had mis-diagnosed: readiness-shaped judgements have no such home. The clearest readiness call of the entire cycle — buy a scoped external pass over an already-passed gate — lives in the T0 emit's final_assessment as prose, indistinguishable from any other sentence and readable back by nothing. So the 3,333 characters were not caused by authoring at the seam; they were caused by three of the six entries having nothing structured to be rendered FROM, and being rewritten from prose scattered across narrative fields. The axis was wrong: not WHEN the record is written but WHICH judgements have a structured home. Replaced with Q-rc04-e, whose standing recommendation is to give readiness judgements the same treatment walk decisions already have — a named slot at the decision point carrying what was decided, which pass tokens it was formed against, and whether the disposition was the AI's own belief or a Sal ratification, which D-rc04-3 as amended now requires be distinguishable. Its open sub-question is which judgements qualify, since buy-another-pass, accept-this-residual, believe-this-is-ready and route-this-expansion are four different shapes that may not want one slot. One residue kept from the retired question: three of rc02c's six warnings genuinely AROSE at the seam — the sync agent's stale cross-reference, the at-archive correction, the touchpoint divergence — and D-rc04-12 already classifies those as process notes rather than readiness, which suggests warnings is their legitimate home and rc04 should not try to absorb them.
